title: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager: assess Microsoft Foundry agents against AI regulations
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing statements and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should flag Microsoft's conflicting assessment-creation role guidance and complete the abbreviated control paths.

claims.claim: The roadmap feature belongs to Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Purview"]

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; summary; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is January CY2027, described as a target rather than a commitment.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is December CY2025.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "December CY2025"

claims.claim: General Availability is a listed roadmap release phase.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: Preview is a listed roadmap release phase.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let customers map agents created in Foundry to compliance regulations and assessments in Compliance Manager.
claims.quote: Customers can map Agents being created in AI Foundry to compliance regulations and assessments in Purview Compliance Manager

claims.claim: The roadmap describes automatically accessing the compliance posture of agents created in AI Foundry.
claims.quote: This feature in Purview Compliance Manager shall enable customers to automatically access the compliance posture of Agents created in AI Foundry.

claims.claim: The planned integration exposes compliance status and improvement actions.
claims.quote: get to know the compliance status and improvement actions to be innovative and compliant.

claims.claim: Learn already describes a Compliance Manager integration using the earlier Azure AI Foundry name.
claims.quote: Compliance Manager integrates with Azure AI Foundry to automate compliance evaluations for AI models and agents.

claims.claim: The documented integration covers AI models.
claims.quote: Compliance Manager integrates with Azure AI Foundry to automate compliance evaluations for AI models and agents.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The integration syncs Foundry agent evaluation results directly into Compliance Manager.
claims.quote: Compliance Manager integrates with Azure AI Foundry to automate compliance evaluations for AI models and agents. The Compliance Manager integration with Azure AI Foundry syncs evaluation results directly into Compliance Manager

claims.claim: Learn describes 75 actions provided by Foundry.
claims.quote: AI Foundry provides 75 actions, including 15 automated evaluation actions

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn identifies 15 automated evaluation actions in the Foundry action set.
claims.quote: AI Foundry provides 75 actions, including 15 automated evaluation actions

claims.claim: The automated evaluation metrics include reliability, BLEU score, coherence and fluency.
claims.quote: 15 automated evaluation actions for metrics like reliability, BLEU score, coherence, and fluency.

claims.claim: Compliance Manager regularly syncs the 15 evaluation actions from Foundry.
claims.quote: Compliance Manager regularly syncs these 15 evaluation actions from AI Foundry

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The synced evaluation actions display pass/fail status.
claims.quote: displaying real-time pass/fail status and detailed metrics.

claims.claim: Compliance Manager displays detailed evaluation metrics alongside compliance status.
claims.quote: Detailed Insights – Provides granular evaluation metrics alongside compliance status for transparency.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users can convert automated Foundry actions to manual actions through Compliance Manager settings.
claims.quote: Flexible Action Management – Users can convert automated actions to manual actions through Compliance Manager settings.

claims.claim: Organizations without Foundry access can update actions manually.
claims.quote: Manual Update Support – Allows manual updates for organizations without AI Foundry access.

claims.claim: The Learn integration passage gives no preview or general-availability status label.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager Foundry integration default enabled automatic assessments; opened compliance-manager-assessments, including the complete Automatic Assessments for AI Apps and Agents section. No integration release-status label appears there.

claims.claim: Compliance Manager is already the tool in which organizations build and manage their assessments.
claims.quote: All of your assessments are listed on the Assessments page Compliance Manager. You can create one assessment that covers multiple services.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the Foundry integration's tenant arrival default or said that arrival changes existing behavior.
claims.quote: Searched: "Foundry" "Compliance Manager" "default"; read roadmap record, compliance-manager-assessments and compliance-manager-setup. Product-wide automatic-testing defaults are stated, but the integration's tenant arrival default is not.

claims.claim: The Foundry actions outside the specified 15 evaluation actions are not described as automated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Compliance Manager" "Foundry" "75" automated manual actions; read compliance-manager-assessments and improvement-actions search excerpts. Foundry's passage identifies 15 automated evaluation actions, not automation for the remaining actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Access to Compliance Manager, including its assessment data, follows its role-based permission model.
claims.quote: Only users who are assigned a role can access Compliance Manager, and the actions allowed by each user are restricted by role type. Our RBAC model also allows you to grant user access to individual assessments.

claims.claim: Users need at least Compliance Manager Reader or Microsoft Entra Global reader to access Compliance Manager.
claims.quote: Users need at least the Compliance Manager reader role, or Microsoft Entra global reader role, to access Compliance Manager.

claims.claim: Access can be granted per assessment through Manage user access.
claims.quote: From your Assessments page, find the assessment you want to grant access to. Select it to open its details page. In the upper-right corner, select Manage user access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Adding Foundry agents during assessment creation requires Azure AI Project Manager or Azure AI User on the relevant Foundry accounts.
claims.quote: The admin account must have either the Azure AI Project Manager or Azure AI User RBAC role assigned to the relevant AI Foundry accounts.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Azure AI User was renamed Foundry User.
claims.quote: Foundry User, Foundry Owner, Foundry Account Owner, and Foundry Project Manager were previously named Azure AI User, Azure AI Owner, Azure AI Account Owner, and Azure AI Project Manager.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Azure AI Project Manager was renamed Foundry Project Manager.
claims.quote: Foundry User, Foundry Owner, Foundry Account Owner, and Foundry Project Manager were previously named Azure AI User, Azure AI Owner, Azure AI Account Owner, and Azure AI Project Manager.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The assessments page lists Compliance Manager Administration, Compliance Manager Assessor or Global Administrator for creating and modifying assessments.
claims.quote: To create and modify an assessment, a user must hold a role of Compliance Manager Administration, Compliance Manager Assessor, or Global Administrator.
claims.fix: After the role list add: 'Microsoft's setup page gives different creation permissions: Compliance Manager Assessor can edit data but cannot create assessments; Compliance Manager Contribution can create assessments.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/compliance-manager-setup#role-types.

claims.claim: Manual testing means a person sets action status rather than relying on automatically detected status.
claims.quote: Improvement actions set for manual testing are actions that you manually test and implement. You set the necessary implementation and test status states
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/compliance-manager-improvement-actions#testing-type for the sentence describing manually entered versus automatically synced action status.

claims.claim: The displayed automated evaluation status depends on the evaluation actions synced from Foundry.
claims.quote: Compliance Manager regularly syncs these 15 evaluation actions from AI Foundry, displaying real-time pass/fail status and detailed metrics.

claims.claim: Compliance Manager is available to organizations with Office 365 and Microsoft 365 licenses.
claims.quote: Compliance Manager is available to organizations with Office 365 and Microsoft 365 licenses

claims.claim: Assessment availability depends on the organization's licensing agreement.
claims.quote: Assessment availability and management capabilities depend on your licensing agreement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The four premium AI templates are EU Artificial Intelligence Act, ISO/IEC 23894:2023, ISO/IEC 42001:2023 and NIST AI RMF 1.0.
claims.quote: Compliance Manager provides four premium regulatory templates [...] EU Artificial Intelligence Act; ISO/IEC 23894:2023; ISO/IEC 42001:2023; NIST AI Risk Management Framework (RMF) 1.0

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Premium regulations require purchase of a license to use them.
claims.quote: The regulations designated as premium require purchase of a license to use them.

claims.claim: Using an AI regulation counts toward purchased premium licenses.
claims.quote: Using an AI regulation counts toward your purchased premium licenses.

claims.claim: Depending on the licensing agreement, an organization might use up to three more premium templates for free.
claims.quote: Depending on your licensing agreement, your organization might be able to use up to three more premium regulatory templates for free.

claims.claim: Licenses for activated regulations are good for one year.
claims.quote: Licenses for activated regulations are good for one year.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Foundry assessments passage says built-in assessments for key AI regulations are free for six months with Copilot or Agent licenses.
claims.quote: Organizations benefit from built-in assessments for key AI regulations—including the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO/IEC standards—provided free for six months with Copilot or Agent licenses.

claims.claim: The Foundry assessments passage does not specify which Copilot or Agent licenses qualify for the six-month offer.
claims.quote: Searched: "Foundry" "assessments" "six months" license price Compliance Manager; read compliance-manager-assessments and returned licensing excerpts. The passage says Copilot or Agent licenses without identifying qualifying SKUs.

claims.claim: The Foundry assessments passage does not explain what happens after the six free months.
claims.quote: Searched: "Foundry" "assessments" "six months" license price Compliance Manager; read compliance-manager-assessments and compliance-manager-regulations. No post-six-month terms are given in the Foundry passage.

claims.claim: The regulation licensing page gives purchase routes but no per-license price on the pages read in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager Foundry integration default enabled automatic assessments Copilot Agent licenses six months pricing meter; read compliance-manager-regulations in full and compliance-manager-assessments. Purchase routes are listed, not per-license prices.

claims.claim: The cited pages describe no Foundry-specific Compliance Manager meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager Foundry integration default enabled automatic assessments Copilot Agent licenses six months pricing meter; read assessments, setup, regulations, Foundry RBAC and resource quickstart. No meter for this integration is described.

claims.claim: Users define the Foundry assessment scope directly in Compliance Manager.
claims.quote: Scoped Assessments – Users define the assessment scope directly in Compliance Manager.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Compliance Manager > Assessments > Add assessment opens the assessment-creation wizard.
claims.quote: From your Assessments page, select Add assessment to begin the assessment creation wizard.
claims.fix: The path opens the right wizard but stops before its creation choices. Extend it to 'Compliance Manager > Assessments > Add assessment > Base your assessment on a regulation > Select regulation > regulation > Add name and group > Select services > Select services > service > Review and finish > Create assessment'. Preserve the note that Foundry agents are added during creation; the page gives no Foundry-specific picker label. See https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/compliance-manager-assessments#create-assessments.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for creating Compliance Manager assessments at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager create assessment API PowerShell New assessment Graph complianceManager assessments; "Compliance Manager" "assessment" "Security & Compliance PowerShell" API. Read assessments and returned references; none creates a Purview Compliance Manager assessment.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Azure portal > Foundry resource > Access control (IAM) reaches Foundry role-assignment management.
claims.quote: In the Azure portal, open your Foundry resource and go to Access control (IAM). Create a role assignment for Foundry User, set Members to User, group, or service principal, select your user principal
claims.fix: Complete the assignment route as 'Foundry resource > Access control (IAM) > Role assignments > Add > Add role assignment > Role > Job function roles > Foundry User > Members > User, group, or service principal > Select members > user'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments-portal for the intermediate steps; retain the Foundry RBAC citation for the role.

claims.claim: az role assignment create --role 53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d --assignee <user> --scope <foundry-resource-id> assigns Foundry User at the specified Foundry resource.
claims.quote: Assign the Foundry User role on your Foundry resource to your user principal. [...] az role assignment create --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" --assignee "joe@contoso.com" --scope /subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/this-rg

claims.claim: 53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d is the Foundry User role definition ID.
claims.quote: Foundry User: 53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d

claims.claim: The command's scope placeholder identifies the relevant Foundry account's Azure resource ID.
claims.quote: Assign the Foundry User role on your Foundry resource to your user principal. [...] Foundry resource: The top-level scope that defines the administrative, security, and monitoring boundary for a Microsoft Foundry environment.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Compliance Manager > Testing source reaches automatic-testing settings.
claims.quote: select the Settings icon at the top of the page, then select Compliance Manager. [...] Select Testing source from the left navigation. [...] Turn off automatic testing for all actions.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Settings > Compliance Manager > Testing source > Turn off automatic testing for all actions'. In the note name the documented alternatives 'Turn on automatic testing for all actions' and 'Turn on automatic testing per action' to preserve the row's general on/off scope. See https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/compliance-manager-setup#testing-source-for-automated-testing.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for the Compliance Manager Testing source setting at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager Testing source automatic testing setting API PowerShell; "Compliance Manager" "Testing source" "PowerShell". Read setup and improvement-actions excerpts; results document portal settings, not an API or cmdlet for this setting.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Compliance Manager settings require Compliance Manager Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: Compliance Manager settings are accessible by users who hold a Compliance Manager Administrator role or Global Administrator role.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Testing source governs automatic testing of eligible improvement actions generally for the organization.
claims.quote: Testing source: Allows you to turn off or on the automatic testing of improvement actions. [...] You can turn off automatic testing for all actions, which disables all automated activity on improvement actions by Compliance Manager.

claims.claim: The Foundry passage does not identify whether its automated-to-manual conversion uses Testing source or another setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager Foundry convert automated actions manual Testing source settings; read assessments, setup and improvement-actions excerpts. Foundry says Compliance Manager settings without naming the conversion control; general Testing type and Testing source options are documented.

claims.claim: Global Administrator or Compliance Manager Administrator can set Compliance Manager user permissions.
claims.quote: The person holding the Global Administrator role or Compliance Manager Administrator role for your organization can set user permissions for Compliance Manager.

claims.claim: Creating a Foundry assessment requires both the relevant Foundry account role and a Compliance Manager role that permits assessment creation.
claims.quote: The Azure AI Project Manager or Azure AI User RBAC role access is required to add Agents during assessment creation [...] To create and modify an assessment, a user must hold a role of Compliance Manager Administration, Compliance Manager Assessor, or Global Administrator.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to take stock of Compliance Manager role holders, but its referenced table row governs assessment creation rather than permissions.
claims.quote: List who holds Compliance Manager Administration, Compliance Manager Assessor or Global Administrator [...] (see the assessment-creation row in the table). [...] Creation of an assessment that includes Foundry agents
claims.fix: Remove the first Before rollout bullet beginning 'List who holds Compliance Manager Administration': the assessment-creation row does not document the permissions control. Do not add a control row.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects premium regulation licenses alongside the six-month Foundry assessment offer with Copilot or Agent licenses.
claims.quote: Using an AI regulation counts toward your purchased premium licenses. [...] built-in assessments for key AI regulations [...] provided free for six months with Copilot or Agent licenses.
